test_title: PYST 42: SSC GD Constable 2022 - General Knowledge (Held On : 30 Jan 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: After the passage of which Constitutional Amendment Act, are there now six fundamental rights?
solution:
The correct answer is __**44th Amendment in 1978.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **44th Amendment Act of 1978** is the Constitutional Amendment Act that reduced the number of fundamental rights from seven to six by removing the right to property as a fundamental right.
 
• **102nd Amendment in 1996** was related to the implementation of the **Mandal Commission report** on reservations in jobs and education for **Other Backward Classes (OBCs).**
 
• 44th Amendment in 1952 **does not exist** as the Constitution of India was adopted in 1950 and the first amendment was made in 1951.
 
• 11th Amendment in 1952 **does not exist** as there were only three amendments made in 1951, which were related to the salaries of the President, Vice-President, and Governors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental rights** are a set of basic rights that are guaranteed to all citizens under the Constitution of India.
 
• These include the** right to equality, freedom of speech and expression, freedom of religion, right to life and liberty,** and** cultural and educational rights.**
 
• The **Right to Education **was added as the** sixth fundamental right** by the** 44th Amendment in 1978**, which made it the responsibility of the state to provide free and compulsory education to all children between the ages of six and fourteen.
 
• The **Right to Education** was further strengthened by the** 86th Amendment in 2002**, which made education a fundamental right for children between the ages of six and fourteen.
 
 
• This amendment also made it mandatory for private schools to **reserve 25% of their seats** for children from economically weaker sections.
